[3] user: Heres a previous analysis of previous junction hackathons: Junction’s recent winners ranged from a four-person team simulating radio waves to a solo builder turning equipment reporting into a game. The pattern I’d take into this weekend is to **pick a specific problem your team can make visible in a working demo**. That matters at Junction because other hackers choose the five overall finalists before the grand jury sees them. [GitHub](https://github.com/ron0studios/WAVELET?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## What won in previous years

| Edition and result | Project | What the team built |
|---|---|---|
| **2025 · Overall and Sensofusion challenge winner** | **WAVELET** | Rudrrayan Manna, Arjun Juneja, Keanu Czirjak and Akshith Alluri built a real-time radio-wave simulator in C++ and OpenGL. Their demo showed waves moving through a 3D model of Hong Kong. They chose a challenge that played to their graphics-programming strengths and used the sponsor’s city dataset. The project used zero AI at an AI-themed edition. [Junction](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/REDACTED?utm_source=chatgpt.com) |
| **2025 · Second overall** | **LoreDash** | Frank Sandqvist used AI to turn Wikipedia articles into playable minigames. It also placed second in its partner track, so a project can finish second overall even if another team wins its track. [hackjunction.com](https://www.hackjunction.com/blog/frank-sandqvist-story?utm_source=chatgpt.com) |
| **2024 · Overall winner** | **BREAKDANCE** | Sandqvist built this one solo. It was an AI-powered inventory app that gamified equipment reporting. He pitched it with an AI-generated rap video, which he felt helped the presentation land. He had been competing at Junction since 2019. [hackjunction.com](https://www.hackjunction.com/blog/frank-sandqvist-story?utm_source=chatgpt.com) |
| **2024 · Second overall** | **Sonaptics** | The team built a gesture-controlled system for reporting issues on an HK Foods production line, where hygiene requirements made a touchless interface valuable. A conversation with the sponsor helped them choose the problem, and their demo combined motion sensors with a real-time interface. [taitounited.fi](https://www.taitounited.fi/blog/menestyst%C3%A4-junction-hackathonista/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) |
| **2023 · Overall winner** | **Driving Change – In the Blink for Safety** | Markus Andersson, David Enberg, Johannes Peltola and Alex Granlund used Pixieray’s glasses sensor data to flag possible signs of driver fatigue from eye and head movements, then combined it with GPS data for a driving review. [en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junction_\(hackathon\)?utm_source=chatgpt.com) |
| **2022 · Overall and Google Cloud side-challenge winner** | **Haru** | Team **Bitter Sweet**, four builders covering ML, backend, frontend and design, made a diary app for teenagers that generated an illustration from each entry. They had already won Junction Asia in Busan with a different project. [The Asia Business Daily](https://view.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2022111311381508794?utm_source=chatgpt.com) |

First-timers can place, too. In 2025, three Aalto colleagues at their first hackathon won Aalto’s challenge out of nearly 30 submissions with **ApprenticeCircle+**, a voice-first platform that matched older and younger adults to share skills. Their prototype made the accessibility idea tangible by letting people create a profile through a phone conversation. [Aalto University](https://www.aalto.fi/en/news/aalto-students-and-researchers-shape-together-how-we-age-with-ai-at-junction-hackathon-2025?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## What you’ll face this weekend

**Junction runs 13–15 November at Hype Areena in Espoo**, with teams of **one to four**. Friday doors open at **16:00**, the opening ceremony is at **18:00**, and hacking starts at **19:30**. Final submissions are due **Sunday at 10:00**, giving you **38½ hours** from kickoff. There’s also a Friday-night preliminary submission. The platform says **23:55** and the event site says **23:59**, so I’d work to **23:55**. All times are local. [2026.hackjunction.com](https://2026.hackjunction.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Partners choose their own challenge winners using their own criteria. Face-to-face peer review selects the **top five overall**, who pitch to the grand jury on Sunday. The published tracks cover hardware, healthcare, AI infrastructure, fintech, agentic AI and data. Some tech challenges can be entered alongside your main track. [2026.hackjunction.com](https://2026.hackjunction.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

I’d use Friday’s sponsor conversations to find out **what they want to see working on Sunday** and which data, hardware or APIs you can actually access that night. Then aim to have **one end-to-end demo by Saturday evening**. For peer review, rehearse a version that starts with the user’s problem and gets to the working prototype in under a minute. If you want a concrete benchmark before Friday, WAVELET’s repository has screenshots and its submission presentation. [WAVELET on GitHub](https://github.com/ron0studios/WAVELET) [Junction](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/REDACTED?utm_source=chatgpt.com). Also I added a new junction guide df to the ~/Downloads directory that elaborates the whole juding process including the important peer review part which makes the isual impressiveness imprnatnt because thats what our peers would find "cool"

user: Heres some info from a side converstaion: We discussed using the Gemini Decisions API alongside standard Gemini to help the system recognize when construction documents lack enough information to answer a question.

user: The proposed starting point is one evidence-sufficiency gate: give Decisions the user’s question and actual source material, then classify it as sufficient, insufficient, or unclear. The prompt should allow answers derived through calculation, while checking that essential facts do not need to be assumed. “Insufficient” applies only to the material inspected; “unclear” should trigger further inspection or clarification rather than automatic refusal.

user: An optional later stage is standard Gemini generates candidate answers and evidence references → Decisions evaluates their support. However, selecting confidently among candidates does not establish that any candidate is correct. Include an unsupported/insufficient option and evaluate against original evidence, not just Gemini’s explanation. Verification should also cover confidently generated answers.

user: We rejected making many checks independent vetoes: false rejections would accumulate and suppress answer coverage. Start with one overall decision; add targeted checks only for demonstrated failure modes.

user: Treat confidence scores as signals to validate on this dataset, not guaranteed probabilities of correctness. Compare the gated pipeline against ordinary Gemini using answer coverage and error rate among answered questions, including deliberately incomplete drawings. The goal is fewer unsupported answers without excessive abstention.
